description: Restore Settings System log-level behavior and Runtime configuration on the .NET server by using supported configuration APIs instead of missing settings endpoints.

tasks.title: Harden settings config API
tasks.spec: specs/http-api/spec.md#Settings configuration API exposes log level
tasks.description: Make the .NET configuration API a reliable contract for issue 19 settings data. Ensure `/api/config` exposes `logLevel` and runtime scheduling keys, `PUT /api/config/logLevel` accepts only `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`, and `ERROR`, and unsupported runtime keys are rejected rather than silently accepted.
acceptanceCriteria: `PUT /api/config/logLevel` persists each supported level and rejects unsupported values with a 400-class validation error without changing the previous value.
`PUT /api/config/{key}` persists supported runtime scheduling keys and rejects unknown keys with a clear error response.
Backend regression tests cover log-level read/update/reject behavior and runtime scheduling key read/update behavior.
tasks.output: Validated .NET settings configuration API and backend tests.
tasks.notes: Keep `/api/config` as the canonical contract; do not add duplicate `/api/log-level` or `/api/agent-runtime` endpoints unless implementation proves the existing contract cannot satisfy the specs.

tasks.title: Restore System log-level control
tasks.spec: specs/web-ui/spec.md#Settings System log level uses supported backend state
tasks.description: Migrate the Web System log-level path away from missing `/api/log-level` calls and onto the supported config API while preserving the existing UI-facing hook shape. The System page must show the persisted log level, persist supported changes, and surface failures visibly instead of silently accepting them.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings > System displays the actual persisted log level from `/api/config` and no longer falls back to hardcoded `INFO` except when `INFO` is the persisted value.
Changing Log Level to `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`, or `ERROR` persists through `PUT /api/config/logLevel` and refreshes the confirmed value.
Failed log-level saves show a visible error notification and do not leave the failed value presented as saved.
The Web settings client no longer requires `/api/log-level` for System log-level load or save on the .NET server.
Web regression tests cover real value loading, successful save, failed save, and supported option rendering.
tasks.output: Working Settings > System log-level UI backed by `/api/config` plus Web tests.
tasks.notes: This task also satisfies `specs/settings-system-diagnostics/spec.md#Settings System log level reflects persisted state` and `specs/settings-system-diagnostics/spec.md#Settings System log level changes are durable and explicit`.

tasks.title: Restore Runtime settings panel
tasks.spec: specs/agent-runtime/spec.md#Agent runtime settings expose effective scheduling configuration
tasks.description: Migrate the Runtime settings read/write path from missing `/api/agent-runtime` calls to a Web settings adapter backed by `/api/config` and `PUT /api/config/{key}`. The panel must load effective scheduling values, persist supported edits and resets, and explicitly disable or explain unsupported fields without failing the entire page.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings > Runtime loads successfully on the .NET server when `/api/config` returns supported runtime scheduling values and no longer shows `Failed to load settings: Empty response from /agent-runtime`.

Runtime displays effective values for concurrency, session timeout, task timeout, stage timeout, poll interval, and grace-period behavior using correct unit conversions between server config and the existing UI model.
Saving changed supported fields writes only supported config keys through `PUT /api/config/{key}`, refetches confirmed state, and shows visible errors on failed writes.
Reset behavior only targets supported fields and does not report success for unsupported fields.
Unsupported or unavailable runtime fields render disabled with explanatory text instead of failing the whole panel or showing misleading persisted defaults.
The Web settings client no longer requires `/api/agent-runtime` for Runtime load or save on the .NET server.
Web regression tests cover load success, load failure, unit conversion, disabled unsupported fields, save success, save failure, and reset behavior.
tasks.output: Working Settings > Runtime panel backed by `/api/config` plus Web tests.
tasks.notes: Keep the adapter in the settings entity API layer so `AgentSettingsSection` can continue consuming the stable `AgentRuntimeConfig` hook contract. Preserve issue non-goals: do not change runtime semantics, liveness checks, or model-selection behavior.
